reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction by Demis Hassabis from 2019 in what I was able to read. The year should be marked quiet. The two likeliest sources from that year had no usable text, so this is a "not found", not proof that he made no prediction.

- **MIT talk, 20 March 2019:** MIT's own page has a captioned transcript. I checked it for words about time, such as years, decades and "within", and found only looks back at earlier work. The text I received stops in the middle of the StarCraft section, so I didn't see the end of the talk or the questions afterwards. Several recent articles say this talk "predicted" AlphaFold and the next five years of AI. Those are later readings of his slides, not his own dated words.
- **DeepMind podcast interview, 17 September 2019:** DeepMind's page for this episode has only a description and a reading list, no transcript. I found no transcript anywhere else.
- **Essay for The Economist's "The World in 2020", November 2019:** a DeepMind post on X quotes it saying AI "could usher in a new renaissance of discovery". That line has no date or time span. The essay itself would not open because the tool rejected the link, so I don't quote from it.
- **2022, not 2019:** a LessWrong post quotes him saying AGI is coming "in the next decade or two". That was in the podcast's second season (episode 9), which came out in early 2022, so it goes under other_years.

In the searches log I count the failed Economist link as one of my six page openings. That makes four openings, and the eleventh search was refused for hitting the tool limit, so it isn't logged.
